verdicts.quote: the first person in line who is eligible (C-37) is booked into the class with no action on their part
the one whose join the app accepted earliest is the first to be offered a freed spot ... the one the app accepted first is ahead ... a freed spot is never taken by a person who is not first in line
Being promoted into one occurrence, or leaving one waitlist, changes no other waitlist entry the member has, including entries for other occurrences at overlapping times.
a member who cancels a booking they received by promotion within 2 hours after being promoted pays none of it ... After the 2 hours the app's normal rules apply.
A spot counts as freed, and C-5 applies, in exactly these cases: (a) a booking stops being active ... every promotion and every entry removal it causes is complete within 60 seconds
goes through every channel the app already uses to confirm bookings ... If a promoted member's notice cannot be delivered, they still hold the booking ... a notice that fails to deliver is retried
no spot is given to two people and none is left free while eligible people are waiting ... After any promotion, an occurrence's active bookings are at most its capacity.
If a member on an occurrence's waitlist comes to hold an active booking in it by any other means ... their entry for that occurrence is removed
verdicts.missing: The race where the first-in-line member themself tries to book directly at the moment they are promoted is not stated: C-15 only refuses 'someone else', so the outcome for that member (refused, or already booked with no second booking) is left open.

verdicts.quote: promotion takes the same amount at the moment of promotion (not at joining) ... If it cannot be taken, the member is skipped under C-17 b and no booking exists.
an occurrence's waitlist holds at most 20 members; the 21st person trying to join is refused ... Otherwise the occurrence shows as full and offers no join control
A waitlist is open until 60 minutes before the class starts ... When it is not open no one can join and no one is promoted.

When staff raise an occurrence's capacity by k, up to k people are promoted, in order ... When staff lower capacity ... no booking is cancelled ... nobody is promoted until the active bookings fall below the capacity.
When staff cancel an occurrence, all its waitlist entries are removed and each member receives the notice in C-22. Nobody is promoted.
each entry's position, member name and the date and time they joined ... At all times positions on a waitlist are the whole numbers 1 to N with no gaps and no repeats.
verdicts.missing: Whether position is stored on the entry or derived from join order, and the entry's set of states, are not stated as a record definition.

verdicts.quote: Within 60 seconds after it closes (C-70), every remaining entry is removed ... remains visible to staff for 90 days after the occurrence's start time, and is then deleted.
show a waitlisted member as waitlisted for that class together with their current position ... A member never sees another member's name or any identifying detail of anyone on a waitlist
sees its waitlist ordered by position ... A staff member removing an entry makes it disappear ... a history of its waitlist events, each with the time, the member's name and exactly one event type
verdicts.missing: Whether staff can promote someone by hand is not stated; no manual-promote action is given or excluded.

verdicts.quote: With the waitlist switched off: no member is shown a join control, every join is refused (C-14 j), no promotion happens ... For each occurrence staff can mark joining closed or open
every promotion and every entry removal it causes is complete within 60 seconds ... no one looking at the occurrence at any moment sees a free spot
For an occurrence with a free spot (and no one waiting), booking works exactly as before the feature ... no booking is changed, added or removed.
When the feature first goes live, every occurrence has an empty waitlist and no booking is changed, added or removed.
